Search the web for articles originally published between 2010 and 2020 (inclusive) on the websites of news publications where a person describes dreaming that they were flying above a town in the desert. Use varied phrasing: "dream* fly* desert town", "flying over/above a desert city/town", named deserts (Mojave, Sonoran, Sahara, Negev, Atacama), and paraphrases ("soaring", "hovering", "dusty desert settlement"). Include interviews, first-person essays, lifestyle/health/psychology/travel sections. Prioritize credible news outlets (newspapers, magazines, digital-native news).

For each potential match, compile: 1) publication name, 2) article title, 3) URL, 4) original publication date (not just last updated), 5) the line(s) describing the dream (quote or paraphrase), 6) identity of the person who had the dream and any age/birth-year evidence in the article or reliable sources, and 7) whether the publication qualifies as a news outlet.

Then, for each publication candidate, verify if at least one co-founder is documented as a university dropout (left before graduating). Provide sources for this claim (e.g., Wikipedia, credible interviews, company pages).

Important checks: - The person’s age in that specific publication year must be 45–55 inclusive (i.e., birth year circa 1955–1975). Use in-article age clues ("age 50", "in his late forties", specific birth year) and cross-reference with the publication date. - Confirm the article was originally published on that publication’s own site (avoid mere reposts/aggregations). - If the page shows multiple dates, identify the original publication date via the site masthead text, citations, or archive.org (Wayback Machine). Use archives if pages are paywalled or moved.

Deliver a structured summary of all plausible candidates you find, including extracted evidence, links, and brief reasoning. List uncertainties (e.g., ambiguous age statements, unclear founding roles or dropout status). Do not filter out borderline cases; include them but flag the issues.
